## Definition

Let \(\{X_n\}_{n\geq 0}\) be a Markov chain.

The transition probability from state \(i\) to state \(j\) is defined as

$$
p(i,j)
=
P(X_{n+1}=j \mid X_n=i).
$$

## Interpretation

The quantity \(p(i,j)\) represents the probability that the chain moves
to state \(j\) at the next step, given that its current state is \(i\).

## Two-step transition probabilities

To move from \(i\) to \(j\) in two steps, the chain may pass through
any intermediate state \(k\). Therefore,

$$
p^{(2)}(i,j)
=
\sum_{k\in S}p(i,k)p(k,j).
$$
